dominant_cause.pinned_mechanism: UserDataPreparer.prepareUserData(0) on user unlock calls prepareUserDataLI -> enforceSerialNumber -> getSerialNumber -> Os.getxattr(path, 'user.serial'). On this virtual guest, /data is mounted on Linux tmpfs in early-ramdisk. Linux kernel 4.19 (mm/shmem.c) only supports security.* and trusted.* xattrs in shmem_xattr_handlers; user.* xattrs were not implemented in tmpfs until Linux 6.6. Calling getxattr returns ENOTSUP (errno 95: Operation not supported on transport endpoint). getSerialNumber only catches ENODATA, rethrowing ENOTSUP as IOException. prepareUserDataLI catches IOException, destroys user data, retries once with allowRecover=false, fails again, and invokes RecoverySystem.rebootPromptAndWipeUserData(context, 'prepareUserData failed for system user'). RecoverySystem delegates to uncrypt (setup-bcb), which fails with 'failed to set bootloader message: failed to find /misc partition' because the virtual machine lacks a /misc partition. RecoverySystem.bootCommand throws IOException('Reboot failed (no permissions?)'), wrapped by prepareUserDataLI in RuntimeException('error rebooting into recovery'). This uncaught RuntimeException on android.fg handler thread crashes system_server outright (T664 raw lines 44738, 61568).

candidate_tmpfs_xattr_class.evidence: Kernel 4.19 mm/shmem.c lacks shmem_user_xattr_handler. Os.getxattr(path, 'user.serial') returns ENOTSUP (errno 95). UserDataPreparer.java:349 only catches ENODATA and rethrows ENOTSUP as IOException.

candidate_misc_partition_absence.evidence: fstab.virt contains only loop0 (/system) and loop1 (/vendor). uncrypt (setup-bcb) fails: 'uncrypt: failed to set bootloader message: failed to find /misc partition', causing RecoverySystem to throw unhandled RuntimeException on android.fg.

candidate_prior_prepare_step_failure.evidence: vold storage.prepareUserStorage completed with 0 errors for all subdirectories (T664 raw lines 43541-43553). enforceSerialNumber was the very first step to fail.

candidate_serial_enforcement_integer_log.evidence: Integer comparison (serialNumber == userInfo.serialNumber) was never reached because Os.getxattr threw ENOTSUP immediately.

candidate_genuinely_corrupt_user0_dir.evidence: User 0 directories /data/user/0, /data/user_de/0, /data/system_de/0, /data/system_ce/0 exist and are valid.

attempted_fix.shape: Candidate Shape 1: Patch UserDataPreparer.getSerialNumber in classes2.dex of services.jar at offset 0x2c33f0: catch (ErrnoException) { return -1; }
attempted_fix.unmasked_wall: Modifying services.jar bytecode changed classes2.dex CRC32 from 0xfa0310b9 to 0xdf90e1bc, causing odrefresh --check to exit with 79 (kCompilationRequired, raw line 5665) and trigger dex2oat64 on-device boot classpath recompilation (raw line 6081). The resulting boot-framework.oat in dalvik-cache caused ZygoteInit to crash with SIGSEGV (SEGV_MAPERR) in art::ArtField::GetDeclaringClass at raw line 7861.

dominant_cause.resolution_recommendation_for_next_lane: Avoid modifying services.jar in system.img to protect ART boot profiles. Instead, mount an ext4 filesystem backed by loopback on /data in early-ramdisk (or format /dev/ram0 using brd). On ext4, getxattr returns ENODATA instead of ENOTSUP, and setxattr succeeds natively.
